artworks.title: Atropos (The Fates)
artworks.description: One of Goya's Black Paintings, painted directly onto the walls of his house, the Quinta del Sordo, and later transferred to canvas. It shows the Fates hovering in a dark sky above a bound human figure, with Atropos bearing the shears that cut the thread of life. It now hangs in the Museo del Prado, Madrid.

artworks.title: A Golden Thread
artworks.description: Strudwick's Pre-Raphaelite allegory gathers the three Fates at their eternal labour: Clotho spins, Lachesis measures, and Atropos waits with the shears that no prayer can stay. The cutting sister — 'she who cannot be turned' — dominates the moral of the golden thread.

artworks.title: Atropos (House of Theseus mosaic, Paphos)
artworks.description: Detail from the Achilles mosaic in the House of Theseus at Paphos: Atropos appears among the Fates attending the hero's infancy, the sister whose shears will one day cut even Achilles' glorious thread. A rare ancient floor image that isolates the cutter by name.

artworks.title: The Three Fates
artworks.description: A circular engraving attributed to Jacob Matham, now in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art: the Moirai share one medallion of distaff, measure and shears. Atropos, the inexorable cutter, completes the triad that Northern print culture spread across early modern Europe.

artworks.title: The Three Fates
artworks.description: Thumann's popular Salon image distinguishes the sisters sharply: Atropos with shears at the ready, young Clotho at the weave, and Lachesis measuring. The cutter of lots becomes the dark accent of a print that circulated widely in the nineteenth century.
